overview:
John Mannion enters the general election as a clear favorite in a central New York district that leans Democratic by four points. He has raised more than seven times as much as Republican Kailee Buller and carries a large cash-on-hand advantage, with no outside spending reported against him. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price his reelection at roughly 95 percent or better.

No public general-election polls are available and no expert raters list the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals: incumbency, the district's Democratic lean, and the fundraising gap. The forecast expects Mannion to win by about seventeen points, with uncertainty widened by the lack of direct polling. A sharp national shift against Democrats or a late Republican funding surge would be needed to make this competitive.
